raw_response:
I'm 60 this year, been farming these 9 mu since I was 15. Didn't go to school much — can read prices and do simple sums, but I don't trust those book numbers. I trust what I've seen with my own two eyes and what my neighbors do.

My wheat went in last October, same week as always, right after National Day. I've got 4 mu of it. I put down base fertilizer then — about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up. I need to topdress. Last year fertilizer got expensive so I cut back to half a bag of urea per mu, and my wheat turned yellow and thin. Only got about 350 jin per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang did the full bag and his was fine. So this year I'm back to 15 kg of urea per mu at green-up, same as always. I'll irrigate twice more before harvest — once when I put the fertilizer down, and once at heading if the sky stays dry. The well electricity keeps going up, but dry wheat means no wheat, so I have to pay.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I have maybe five or six days to get the maize in. Very tight. I plant 4 mu of hybrid maize, same seed as last year. I hire Lao Zhang's tractor to plow right after harvest — 50 yuan per mu, but I can't do it by hand fast enough. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 20 kg per mu, then topdress another 10 kg of urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations for maize in summer is usually enough, unless July is very dry. My son helps with planting when he's not working construction in town. Me and my wife do the rest.

Cotton is on 3 mu. I plant in late April. Cotton needs watching — I plow in early April and put down base fertilizer, then another handful at flowering. I irrigate twice. The bollworm was bad two years ago so I keep some insecticide ready. Picking is all family labor — me, my wife, and my daughter helps on Sundays. Three or four picks from September to October. Hard on the back, but the cotton price was decent last year so I keep doing it.

Watermelon is 2 mu. My wife pushed for it — sells well at the market in town if the price holds. I plant early May. I got a cartload of chicken manure cheap from the poultry farm down the road — 100 yuan — so I mix that with compound fertilizer. Watermelon drinks a lot of water, so I irrigate three times. Need to watch for fungus when it's humid. If I get 2500 kg per mu and sell at a decent price, it helps with the school fees for my grandson. But last year the price at the gate was low, so you never know.

Money is the big problem. Everything costs more this year. I buy the wheat fertilizer now because the crop is already in the ground. Cotton and watermelon fertilizer I'll buy in April. Maize seed and fertilizer I'll get in May. I don't hire labor except for the tractor — family does everything else. Better to spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing half the crop. My father always said a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and I've seen enough bad years to know he's right.
